subject: Noble Health - request: audit log retention exception & backup purge alignment
messages:
From: Compliance Team <audit@noblehealth.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: audit log retention exception & backup purge alignment

Hi Mina,

We're preparing for an upcoming regulated audit and need to request a temporary exception for retention of detailed audit logs and a guarantee around backup purge timelines. Per our DPA, our default retention is 12 months, but the audit scope will require 18 months for access to full system logs and snapshot state.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood extend log retention for Noble account to 18 months for audit-readonly access?
- Can you confirm whether backups that are scheduled for monthly purge can be paused or tagged to prevent deletion during the audit period (audit window: 2027-09-15 to 2028-03-15)?
- We need an audit-friendly runbook describing deletion workflows, who performs restores, and a point of contact for legal/eDiscovery.

Attached: initial DPA amendment request and our SOC2 scoping note.

Thanks,
Sophie Lin
Senior Compliance Manager
Noble Health
attachments: Noble_DPA_retention_request.pdf (application/pdf), soc2-snapshot-2027-06.pdf (application/pdf)

From: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Compliance Team <audit@noblehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit log retention exception & backup purge alignment

Hi Sophie — thanks for sending this over. We're happy to help and want to be precise about the operational and legal controls. Quick summary of next steps below and a couple of clarifying questions:

What we can offer now (prelim):
- Temporary retention extension: we can create an account-level retention tag that prevents routine deletion for an 18-month window. This will be implemented via our snapshot lifecycle policy and KV/log-store retention settings.
- Backup purge pause: we can flag monthly backups to be exempt from automated purge; those snapshots will move to a secured hold state.
- Runbook: we'll draft an "audit access & restore runbook" that documents deletion workflows, restore SLAs, and authorized operators.

Clarifying questions:
1) Do you need full-text request-level logs (token-level traces) or higher-level audit events (auth, config changes, model/route calls)? Token-level traces are considered sensitive — we'll need an explicit scope in the DPA.
2) Who at Noble is the legal signatory for a minor DPA amendment vs. an internal compliance acknowledgment?

I'll loop in Kimberly (security/compliance) and Aditya (infrastructure) to scope implementation and timelines. I'll propose a draft runbook by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-runbook-noble-v1.md (text/markdown)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Compliance Team <audit@noblehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit log retention exception & backup purge alignment

Folks — quick technical summary to confirm constraints and options. Quoted below is Mina's note.

- Scope of logs: If Noble needs token-level traces we must treat them as PD and they will remain encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys. We can support export for audit purposes but only under a signed DPA amendment that specifically authorizes export and provides an auditor NDA.
- Implementation plan for retention + hold:
  * Create retention tag (policy: 18 months) at account-scope.
  * Migrate monthly backups matching Noble_* snapshot naming to "audit-hold" storage class; item-level metadata will include hold-until timestamp.
  * Disable automated purge for flagged snapshots. Purge will remain disabled unless a legal/unhold request is submitted by Noble's authorized contact.
- Log access model: read-only exports via secure SFTP or time-limited signed link. No console-level broad listing.

Risks / notes:
- Extra storage cost will accrue; we should capture whether Noble expects a credit/discount for the added retention.
- Cross-border transfer: if any snapshots are stored in multiple regions, we need to ensure transfer mechanisms are DPA-compliant.

I'll draft the exact API calls and an implementation ETA (target: 5 business days after DPA amendment is signed).

-Kim
Principal PM, Security
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Compliance Team <audit@noblehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-09T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit log retention exception & backup purge alignment

Thanks — implementation details from infra side:

Planned steps (implementation runbook excerpt):
1) Create account retention policy via internal config: POST /admin/accounts/noble/policies {retention_months: 18, tag: "audit_hold_202709"} (ops-only).
2) Identify snapshots: list snapshots with tag prefix "noble_2027" and atomically set storageClass=HOLD and disableExpire=true.
3) KV/log-store: set per-collection retention override for event_audit and auth_audit collections. Token-trace collections require manual export flow.
4) Backup purge scheduler: add whitelist filter for hold-tag to bypass the weekly purge job.
5) Audit export: generate encrypted tarball, upload to s3://redwood-secure-exports/noble/202709 and create time-limited (72h) signed URL.

Ops ETA: 3 business days after legal signs amendment and we receive authorized unhold contact. I'll include rollback instructions and an audit log of all operations in the runbook.

-Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Cc: procurement@globemed.com
Date: 2027-09-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit log retention exception & backup purge alignment

Mina / Kim / Aditya —

Thanks for the quick responses and the clear plan. A few clarifications from Noble:
- Scope: We only need event-level data (auth, config, admin actions). We do NOT need token-level traces. That should remove the KMS/export complexity for most items.
- Billing: Noble accepts incremental storage billing for the hold period; we do NOT expect a credit. Please send a simple statement of expected monthly delta so our procurement team can sign off.
- Authorized unhold contact: Sophie Lin (me) and Daniel Cho (legal@NobleHealth.com). Both will be authorized signatories.

Please proceed to draft the DPA amendment language that lists the retention override, hold procedures, export constraints, and an explicit timeline (18 months from the date of hold). We can sign the amendment electronically.

Best,
Sophie
